status: Operational conventions fixed before development outcomes
graphs: Vertices are lexicographically sorted tuples or RNA codons. Edges are Hamming distance one. Independent-set vertices have no consecutive ones. Leucine is CUA, CUC, CUG, CUU, UUA, UUG under the standard code; product edges change one component by one nucleotide.
heat_field: exp(-L) times independent standard normal scores, unnormalized graph Laplacian L and time 1. Floating point eigendecomposition constructs a score field only; subsequent binary graph certificates are exact.
coordinate_fields: Binary coordinates are encoded -1 and +1. Additive coefficients are independent standard normal. Pairwise fields contain independently drawn main and all pair coefficients. Median ties are retained. Endpoints are forced present after thresholding. Forcing endpoint occupancy is an edit, so additive-derived occupancy is not asserted to remain an exact additive superlevel restriction.
initial_observations: Endpoints plus floor((n-2)/4) nonendpoints for the quarter-observed condition. Initial permutation is independent of outcomes and shared across field families for each graph and seed.
seed_streams: numpy PCG64 with SeedSequence([seed,graph_index,family_index,stream_index]). Fields use stream 0; initial subsets use family index 0 and stream 1; random policy uses stream 2. The same random-policy stream is restarted for each initial-observation condition.
degree_policy: Largest degree in the original baseline graph among unknown vertices, then lowest vertex index.
path_midpoint_policy: Unknown vertex nearest the midpoint of the complete shortest possible path, then lowest vertex index. This differs from taking the midpoint of only the unknown subsequence. Its historical internal key is lazy_bisection; the reporting label is Path midpoint, since it differs from the published LazySP bisection selector.
canonical_bisection_policy: Additional sixth baseline specified in acquisition_bisection_amendment_v1.json. Choose the unknown vertex whose path position has maximum distance to the nearest already evaluated path position, with endpoints evaluated, then lowest vertex index. This is a vertex adaptation of Dellin and Srinivasa 2016 Algorithm 2.
path_cut_policy: First query uses bisection, second uses the lowest indexed member of a minimum unknown separator, and so on. Tied minimum separators use the lexicographically smallest sorted vertex set, obtained with exact integral capacities.
clairvoyant_bound: Minimum number of additional true observations sufficient for a certificate, conditional on the actual full truth and initial observations. Computed for every world by a shortest path or negative-vertex cut.
minimax_bound: Q3 only. Exact recurrence over all ternary partial assignments with endpoints present. It is a worst case reference, not a pointwise lower bound on the cost in an individual truth world.
development: Seeds 1000 through 1009 only. No outcome-dependent policy tuning or graph exclusions. The executed development sources were committed at 1e1259477f116ebdc1d69a903bb1552c5c2c92b6 before adding the validation interface.
coverage: Seven graphs; six field families on each of five binary-coordinate graphs and four on each of two leucine graphs; two initial conditions. The original five policies retain their development receipt of 760 worlds and 3800 policy evaluations. The additional canonical bisection policy is separately evaluated on those same 760 development worlds. Fifty heldout seeds 2000 through 2049 give 3800 worlds and 22800 policy evaluations across all six policies.
validation_uncertainty: For each baseline, compute the mean paired query difference within each of 50 complete seed blocks, each with the fixed mix of 76 worlds. Report its mean, standard error across seed blocks and an approximate 95% Student t interval with 49 degrees of freedom. Intervals concern only mean paired differences and Monte Carlo design uncertainty, not biological populations, graph populations, medians, extremes or simultaneous comparisons.
validation_guard: Before generating any heldout fields, require exact source, protocol and software matches to validation_freeze.json. The root must commit the freeze before execution. Results must use a new output directory; under the bounded runner use a new child results directory.
